title: Per-token Emission Waterfall & Adaptive Cache Chargeback
creator: Morgan Lee
description:
Goal: Produce an end-to-end instrumentation and analysis pipeline that attributes request latency and cost down to individual emitted tokens, explicitly quantifying the impact of KV/prefix cache hits versus cold generation. This ticket implements a stable event surface (waterfall slices) and adaptive cache chargeback model used by billing, SLO reconciliation, and latency dashboards.

Background:
- Current observability gives request-level and coarse token aggregates but cannot reliably answer: "Which tokens caused cache misses that drove tail latency?" or "How much of this request's GPU time should be charged to cached vs non-cached execution?"
- We need precise attribution for: performance regressions, per-customer cost analysis (Redwood Dedicated), and automatic rollback triggers for model/runtime changes.

Scope / Deliverables:
1) Instrumentation hooks in the runtime to emit per-token "emission_slice" events with stable schema (see telemetry schema below). These events are emitted at emission completion for each token and include timing of kernel execution, KV lookup latency, cache-hit boolean, sequence slot, and micro-batching context.
2) A lightweight sampler to emit full micro-timings (microsecond-resolution) for 1% of requests; aggregated histograms for all requests.
3) Offline pipeline additions (metrics/logs) to join emit events with request traces and KV cache events to compute: token-level latency, cumulative request waterfall, and cache-influence delta (time saved/penalty).
4) Adaptive chargeback algorithm implemented in the ingestion pipeline that apportions GPU and host CPU time to tokens based on measured kernel time and an MVCC-style attribution when multiple requests share cache entries.
5) Dashboards: per-model and per-route waterfall explorers with token-level hover details, a cache-impact summary panel, and SLO KPI cards highlighting regressions attributable to cache misses.
6) API for downstream consumers (billing, SLO reconcilers) to pull token-attribution aggregates by model, route, and time-window.

Telemetry schema (stable strings/keys):
- event: emission_slice
- fields: [request_id, trace_id, timestamp_iso, token_index, token_text, model_id, route, kernel_ns, kv_lookup_ns, kv_hit, batch_size, shard_id, host_cpu_ns, gpu_ns, seq_len, quantization_mode, sampling_rate_tag]
- event: kv_lookup
- fields: [request_id, trace_id, timestamp_iso, kv_key_hash, hit_boolean, lookup_ns, backend_latency_ns, shard_id]
- all fields are required-as-strings in the emitted JSON envelope; numeric values are sent as strings to avoid schema conversion issues in legacy pipeline

Adaptive chargeback (high-level):
- For tokens with kv_hit=true: compute baseline_lookup_ns = p50(kv_lookup_ns) for the model & shard; token_charge_ns = max(0, kernel_ns + host_cpu_ns - baseline_lookup_ns * hit_credit_factor).
- For kv_hit=false: token_charge_ns = kernel_ns + host_cpu_ns + measured_kv_penalty_ns.
- When multiple requests share a cache warmup (same prefix), use backfilled attribution windows and proportional splitting based on token_order and observed concurrency. Edge cases documented below.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits emission_slice for >=95% of requests (sampled full-microtimings for 1%, summarized histograms for all).
- Ingestion pipeline computes per-token chargeback aggregates within 10s of ingestion and makes them queryable by the dashboard API.
- Dashboards display a token-level waterfall for a request and surface top-5 tokens contributing to tail P95 latency per model.
- Chargeback numbers reconcile to existing per-request GPU/host totals within 3% on average (sanity check).
- Documentation: PRD, schema docs, rollout playbook, and a postmortem template are published in Confluence.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Volume: per-token events are high-cardinality. Mitigation: default sampling + summarized histograms; enforce field-level cardinality limits (no unbounded token_text retention).
- Privacy: token_text might contain sensitive data. Mitigation: token_text is hashed by default; allow opt-in plaintext logging with customer consent and DLP controls.
- Attribution ambiguity for shared cache warmups. Mitigation: deterministic proportional split + diagnostic traces for manual review.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Feature branch + unit tests; runtime hook behind feature flag.
- Week 1: Canary runtime in staging, pipeline consumer reads test-topic; validate schema and storage.
- Week 2: Enable sampled full-microtimings in staging; iterate dashboards.
- Week 3: Gradual production rollout with 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% sampling ramp, monitor pipeline lag and SLOs.
- Post-rollout: 4-week observation window, compare chargeback reconciliation, tune baseline_lookup_ns estimator.

Notes: This ticket intentionally separates the per-token emit surface from downstream aggregation logic so the runtime change can be reviewed and merged independently.

ingestion pipeline computes token_charge_ns aggregates and exposes API within 10s
dashboards show token-level waterfall and top-5 token impact per model

2026-02-18 Jonas Müller: Implementation note — kernel_ns resolution limited by cupti/ROCm timers; we'll normalize to microseconds in runtime to reduce noise. Added probe shim in runtime. (see PR #7842)

2026-02-25 Data infra: Pipeline team confirmed support for numeric-as-string fields; asked to include schema version header for forward compatibility.

2026-03-01 Priya Patel: Started staging canary; emission events flowing to observability-topic. Initial end-to-end test shows ingestion latency ~4.2s for sampled requests. Next: reconcile chargeback to nightly job.
